*Odin's single eye fixes upon Thor with the weight of ages, his grip tightening on Gungnir as he leans forward on Hlidskjalf*

Thor. The frost giants have sent envoys. They say you razed the Temple of Thrym during what was meant to be a peaceful passage. The truce I brokered with King Thrym's heirs cost Asgard two centuries of negotiation. You knew the terms. 

Explain yourself — and understand that "they provoked me" will not suffice.

*His voice echoes through the hall, carrying both the authority of the Allfather and the disappointment of a father*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I know. I was mistaken. There were other things, more pressing, that led me to act. My desire to protect Asgard and its people from threats within and without. I was not aware that my actions would break the truce. But I will make amends, I will make it right.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*Odin's eye narrows, his fingers drumming once upon the armrest of his throne*

"Not aware?" Thor, you are not some green warrior fresh from his first skirmish. You have walked the Nine Realms for over a thousand years. The Temple of Thrym stands — stood — at the very heart of their sacred grounds. Its destruction could not be mistaken for anything less than a deliberate act of war.

*He rises slowly from Hlidskjalf, his presence filling the hall*

You speak of threats "within and without," yet you give me no substance. What threat could possibly justify razing a temple during peaceful passage? What enemy lurked there that required Mjolnir's fury rather than a word to your king and father?

And amends? Do you think you can simply rebuild stone and ice? The Jotun measure honor in centuries, not apologies. King Thrym's heirs have already sent word that they consider the truce void.

*His voice drops lower, more dangerous*

Tell me what truly happened, my son. Not what you wish had happened. Not vague words about "pressing matters." The truth — before I must make decisions neither of us will welcome.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Asgard. They have come to Asgard. And they have brought death and destruction in their wake. Cities laid to ruin, lives lost. They seek to conquer our realms, to bring about the end of days. They cannot be allowed to succeed. We must stop them at any cost.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*Odin descends the steps of Hlidskjalf with deliberate slowness, each footfall echoing like thunder*

Who, Thor? WHO has come to Asgard? 

*He stops directly before his son, Gungnir planted firmly on the golden floor*

I sit upon the high seat that sees all Nine Realms. Heimdall stands eternal watch at the Bifrost. The walls of Asgard remain unbreached. Our cities stand whole. No alarm has been raised, no horn sounded. Yet you speak of ruin and conquest as if Ragnarok itself pounds at our gates.

*His voice sharpens like a blade*

You went to Jotunheim days ago. If such devastation had occurred in your absence, you would have been summoned back instantly. If it happened before you left, the realm would be mobilized for war — not sending its prince on what was supposed to be a diplomatic passage.

*Odin's single eye burns with the need for truth*

I will ask you once more, and I will know if you lie to me, Thor Odinson. What threat did you perceive at the Temple of Thrym that made you break two centuries of hard-won peace? Not prophecy. Not fear of what might come. What did you actually encounter that made you raise Mjolnir against sacred ground?

transcript.text: I understand the consequences now, the weight of my actions. But I cannot simply ignore what lies ahead. The Frost Giants pose a threat, a threat to all of the realms. We must confront this threat together, Asgard, Jötunheim, and beyond. It is my duty to protect my people, even if it means breaking the truce.

transcript.text:
*Odin's patience visibly frays, his voice rising like a storm*

ENOUGH with these evasions! You speak in circles, Thor — "threats ahead," "what lies ahead," yet you destroyed the temple DAYS ago for reasons you still refuse to name!

*He strikes Gungnir against the floor, the sound reverberating through Asgard itself*

You claim the frost giants are a threat that justified your actions, yet now you say we must unite WITH Jotunheim against some greater enemy? Which is it? Are they the danger, or are they our necessary allies? Your words contradict themselves!

*Odin's voice drops to something cold and terrible*

I have ruled for five thousand years, my son. I have fought in wars that would break your mind to witness. I have made sacrifices you cannot fathom. And in all that time, I learned one truth above all others: a king who acts on impulse, who cannot articulate WHY he does what he does, is not a king at all — he is a berserker with a crown.

*He steps closer, eye to eye with Thor*

One. Final. Chance. What happened at the Temple of Thrym? Not prophecy. Not philosophy. Not duty. What did you see, hear, or encounter that made you unleash Mjolnir? If you cannot answer this simple question, then you are either lying to me... or lying to yourself.

You still do not answer the question.

*He turns away, walking back toward Hlidskjalf with measured steps*

Five times I have asked you what happened at that temple. Five times you have given me everything BUT an answer. Noble words about unity. Vague warnings about threats. Apologies without substance. This is not the bearing of a warrior who acts with conviction — this is the floundering of one who knows he erred but cannot admit why.

*He seats himself once more upon the throne, and his voice carries the weight of judgment*

Very well. Since you cannot — or will not — tell me the truth, I shall tell you what I suspect. You went to Jotunheim with old grudges burning in your heart. Perhaps you saw frost giants training. Perhaps they spoke words that pricked your pride. Perhaps nothing happened at all save your own restlessness and the hammer's weight in your hand. And in a moment of rage, you destroyed what took two centuries to build.

*His eye fixes on Thor with terrible certainty*

You have no great threat to report. You have no intelligence of invasion. You destroyed the temple because you WANTED to, and now you scramble for justifications that might make it seem noble.

Am I wrong, my son? Then prove it. Give me one concrete fact about this threat you claim to face.

My son. You have destroyed a sacred temple. You have broken a truce that cost me two centuries. And now, when pressed for truth, you fabricate an invasion that does not exist. This is not the behavior of Asgard's protector — this is madness or deception, and I do not yet know which is worse.

Strip away the false words. Tell me TRUE — what demons plague your mind that you would do this?
